## Summary

3.2.0 judges a fine-grained personal access token by its grant and a `read_api` token by what GitLab accepts from it, action by action. It builds with Go 1.27.2 and `golang.org/x/net` v0.60.0 for the Go security advisories of 2026-10-08, and its binaries no longer carry `golang.org/x/crypto`.

- A fine-grained token is read as a grant rather than a scope list (#1138). The server withholds the actions no fine-grained token can reach (#1145), and when the token may read its own grant and the instance runs the GitLab release the permission table was recorded from, it lists only the actions the grant reaches and answers a call it does not with the permission GitLab names for it (#1146; ADR-0024).
- A `read_api` token is served the actions GitLab accepts from it, derived from the requests each action sends, rather than every action annotated read-only (#1245; ADR-0026). Each action's page in the tool reference states the classic scope and the fine-grained permissions it needs (#1246).
- The legacy HTTP gate admits a token at the `read_api` minimum, and refuses one below it with a 403 that costs no authentication budget (#1159). A stdio process whose token carries neither `read_api` nor `api` refuses each catalog request (#1160).
- `GITLAB_MCP_YOLO_MODE` and `AUTOPILOT` now skip the confirmation of a destructive action on the default dynamic surface too, as they did on the meta and individual surfaces (#1214).
- The Claude Desktop extension ships one bundle per operating system, 59% to 80% smaller to download than the single bundle, which is still published for the links that point at it (#1124). The NuGet packages are attested (#1123), and every package carries the licence and the third-party notices (#1125).
- The user documentation lives on the site, in English and Spanish, with a tool reference generated from the action catalog (#1191, #1193). client-go v3.15.0 (#1177).

## Breaking changes

None to configuration. Three changes an operator or a client may notice:

- A stdio `GITLAB_TOKEN` with neither `read_api` nor `api` (a `read_user`, `read_repository` or `self_rotate` token, say) is refused every catalog request, and `--ignore-scopes` does not lift it (#1160). Such a token could not read the REST API before either; every call it made failed with GitLab's 403.
- Log lines that named a credential by its last four characters (`token_suffix`) now name it by `credential_hash`, a keyed digest that changes with every restart and differs between replicas (#1220).
- The output schema of the meta tools and of `gitlab_execute_action` names the pagination total `total_items`, the field every list result already carried, instead of `total` (#1215).

Withdrawn, as the versioning policy allows in a minor release for what a tool could never honor:

- `open_issues_count`, `closed_issues_count` and `open_merge_requests_count` wherever GitLab sends no counts, where they read 0 (#1217): on `project.label_get`, `project.label_create`, `project.label_update` and `project.label_subscribe`, on their group twins `group.group_label_get`, `group.group_label_create`, `group.group_label_update` and `group.group_label_subscribe`, and on `project.label_list` and `group.group_label_list` called without `with_counts`, which still publish the counts GitLab sends when called with it. The single-label resources `gitlab://project/{project_id}/label/{label_id}` and `gitlab://group/{group_id}/label/{label_id}` stop publishing `open_issues_count` and `open_merge_requests_count`, whose routes never send them.

## Upgrading

1. A deployment that serves fine-grained tokens needs no new setting. Which permissions let the server read a token's grant, and what it serves when it cannot, is on the fine-grained tokens page: <https://docs.jmrp.io/gitlab-mcp-server/operations/fine-grained-tokens/>.
2. Log queries keyed on `token_suffix` move to `credential_hash`.
3. Claude Desktop users can install the bundle for their own system from the release assets; `gitlab-mcp-server.mcpb` remains for all three.
4. A client that read a label's counts from a single label, where they were always 0, reads them from `project.label_list` or `group.group_label_list` with `with_counts`.

## Security

- No vulnerability of this project with an advisory or a CVE is fixed in this release.
- Dependencies: Go 1.27.2 and `golang.org/x/net` v0.60.0 (#1265) fix the thirteen advisories of 2026-10-08 that govulncheck found reachable from this repository's code: GO-2026-6599, GO-2026-6600, GO-2026-6603, GO-2026-6604, GO-2026-6605, GO-2026-6607, GO-2026-6608, GO-2026-6609, GO-2026-6610, GO-2026-6611, GO-2026-6612, GO-2026-6613 and GO-2026-6617. Five of them are in the HTTP/2 implementation that HTTP mode serves with TLS and that the client to GitLab negotiates; #1265 says which of them the server binary reaches, and how.
- The binaries no longer record `golang.org/x/crypto` (#1122). The telemetry keyring derives its keys with the standard library's `crypto/hkdf`, which gives the same keys, so scanners that judge by module stop reporting GO-2026-5932, the unmaintained `openpgp` package that no binary has linked since 3.0.0. CI and the release workflow now check every release binary against the vulnerability database at module grain, the release before anything is published (#1122, #1127).
- Hardening without an advisory: a credential is no longer written to the logs in part (#1220).
